messages:
sara: noticing a ~30% throughput dip on gpu-pool-us-west-2 starting ~03:40UTC, lots of worker restarts. stack traces point to OOM during small bursts. filing here to coordinate :warning:
leo: on it. initial metrics? latency vs p50/p95?
maria: p50 fine, p95 up from 120ms -> 360ms, tail tokens/sec down 28%. error rate 5xx increased, mostly OOM.
aj: curious if this is the kv-cache eviction churn we saw last week. any correlation with kernel switch logs?
sara: good call — attaching the short profiler snippet I grabbed from one affected host:```
[2023-08-11T03:39:58Z] kernel_select: chosen=fastpath_int8 v=1.2 seq_len=128 active_batches=3
[2023-08-11T03:40:01Z] kernel_select: chosen=slowpath_fp16 v=1.2 seq_len=256 active_batches=1
[2023-08-11T03:40:03Z] kvcache: evict start reason=pressure reclaimed=12MB
[2023-08-11T03:40:04Z] allocator: OOM while allocating 64MB (slab=large)
[2023-08-11T03:40:05Z] worker: restart pid=8423 exit=OOM
```
leo: that kernel flip from int8 fastpath -> fp16 slowpath at 03:40 looks suspicious — switching increases memory working set and disables quantized kernels. why did it flip?
maria: sequence length jump to 256 triggered fallback, but active_batches dropped — could be the routing policy misclassified a burst as high-quality (longer seq) and routed to a kernel variant that uses more memory.
aj: also: kvcache reclaim happened right before the OOM. If the kernel change expands per-request KV footprint, combined with aggressive evict, fragmentation could block a contiguous allocation.
leo: I'm seeing allocator fragmentation metrics on the host: free_slab_frag=0.42, largest_free_chunk=18MB, required_contig=64MB. that matches failed allocation.
sara: so flow is: routing -> kernel choice -> increase per-request contig requirement -> allocator cannot satisfy -> OOM -> worker restart -> throughput drop.
maria: mitigation idea: temporarily pin kernel selection to fastpath_int8 on this pool, and throttle long-seq routing for 10m to drain.
leo: I can push a rollback on the kernel routing policy to force fastpath_int8 for the affected node tag. want me to do it?
sara: yes, please. also throttle prefetch window and kvcache reclaim aggressiveness.
leo: triggering policy change now. deploy-bot: started rollout of routing-pin fastpath_int8 -> pool:gpu-pool-us-west-2 nodes:tag=highmem scope=10m
infra-bot: notice: applied kernel routing override to 7 nodes in gpu-pool-us-west-2. monitor p95 and worker restarts.
maria: initial post-change numbers: p95 down to 180ms, worker restarts stopped after 45s, reclaim events reduced. throughput recovering.
aj: follow-up: we should add a guard to kernel selector so it avoids switching to memory-heavier kernels when per-host largest_free_chunk < 2x required_contig. prevents fragmentation-induced OOM.
leo: agreed. I'll open a short PR to kernel selector heuristics with that safeguard and a telemetry counter for "kernel_switch_blocked_by_contig".
sara: also add an eval to simulate sudden long-seq bursts to test routing heuristics under kvcache pressure.
maria: postmortem action items? quick list: 1) temporary pining + throttle (done) 2) kernel selector contig guard (assigned to leo) 3) kvcache reclamation backoff tweak (assigned to aj) 4) add test harness for mixed seq-length bursts (assigned to maria) 5) alert rule for repeated kernel flips on a host (assigned to sara).
aj: I'll take #3 and start a canary. question: do we want to surface kernel flip frequency in Console? could help ops detect pre-oom states.
sara: yes, surface it under per-node perf with a short-term heatmap. small UX but high signal.
leo: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/kernel-selector/pulls/471 (adds contig guard + metric). tagging @sara for review.
maria: leaving this thread open for a bit while we watch metrics. great catch, team. :raised_hands:
